# Review Findings — Atlas Remit / Atlas Direct

## A. Customer-facing promises beyond Elva's catalogue or approved scope

**1. Tron wallet screening — not in the catalogue at all**
> "NUSD payouts that Atlas routes over Tron will also have the receiving wallet screened in real time before funds are released, so your Indonesian partners are covered from day one."
— **AR-04** (proposal)

CAP-021 only defines SG coverage for Ethereum and Polygon/NUSD. Tron does not appear anywhere in the schema. Per the catalogue's `unlisted_rule`, an absent network "cannot be sold under a named exception; only changing or withdrawing the promise resolves it." Elva's own deal desk confirms this: "Tron (any asset, any mode) | Not in catalogue … Not offered" (**AR-05**, row 3). The promise was made to the customer anyway, with no approval mechanism available to cure it.

**2. Payout ledger connector sized above the catalogue limit without an approved exception**
> "The payout ledger connector will be provisioned for 30,000 payouts daily from launch."
— **AR-04**, repeated at **AR-06** §4.1: "support up to thirty thousand (30,000) payouts per day"

CAP-023 caps SG at `max_payouts_per_day: 25,000`. Deal desk flags exactly this: "Proposal sizing is 30,000/day. No approval on file for volume above the limit" (**AR-05**, row 5). The commitment was made to the customer and then carried straight into the draft SOW with no exception on record.

**3. Behavioural-intelligence (fraud signal) connector committed without a valid named approval**
> "Elva will ingest the device and behavioural risk scores from your existing behavioural-biometrics vendor and make them available to fraud rules and investigators from go-live."
— **AR-04**

CAP-027 is beta/`requires_named_approval` in SG. As of **AR-02** (7 Oct), Elva's own solutions consultant said "I'd need to check what we can commit to before I say yes" — i.e., unresolved. By the time of the proposal (16 Oct) it is stated as an unconditional commitment, yet the only approval on file is described in **AR-05** row 4 as "approved in principle on deal desk call … Approver: not recorded" — materially weaker than the properly minuted Polygon exception (row 2, named approver, forum minute). A firm go-live promise rests on an undocumented approval for a beta capability.

**4. Polygon real-time screening promised before the named exception existed**
> "Recipient wallets on both Ethereum and Polygon will be screened in real time, ahead of release, for every NUSD payout."
— **AR-04**, dated 16 October 2026

CAP-021 shows Polygon real-time as beta/`requires_named_approval`. The named exception was only approved on **18 October 2026** (PF-2026-41, per **AR-05** row 2) — two days *after* this unconditional promise was made to the customer. It was later regularised in the SOW, but the proposal itself exceeded approved scope at the moment it was sent.

## B. Firm, specific promises missing or changed in the draft agreement without explicit withdrawal

**5. Tron promise dropped from the SOW/contract, customer still relying on it**
Annex 1 of **AR-06** lists only Ethereum (1.1) and Polygon (1.2) — Tron is absent, with no clause stating it is excluded or withdrawn. Yet the customer email confirms ongoing reliance:
> "Our compliance plan for the Indonesian corridor assumes Tron payouts are screened in real time exactly as your proposal describes."
— **AR-08**

Combined with the entire-agreement clause (**AR-07** §15), Melissa's team believes a commitment is live that will be contractually extinguished on signature unless this is actively corrected with Atlas.

**6. Automatic STR drafting promised, then omitted from the SOW**
> "Suspicious transaction reports will be drafted automatically from the case record, ready for your MLRO to review and file."
— **AR-04**

This is in-catalogue (CAP-015, GA/standard), so deliverable — but **AR-06** contains no clause describing SAR/STR drafting anywhere in its sections. The customer has built process around it and says so explicitly:
> "My MLRO team has built its STR process around the automatic drafting you showed us, so we are counting on that being there at go-live."
— **AR-08**

With the entire-agreement clause in **AR-07** §15 superseding "all prior proposals," this specific, relied-upon commitment risks disappearing unless written into the SOW.

**7. Fraud/behavioural signal ingestion promised, then omitted from the SOW**
As in item 3, **AR-04** firmly promised ingestion of behavioural scores "from go-live." **AR-06** and **AR-07** contain no clause on this capability at all. Customer reliance is explicit:
> "Joel's team is planning the fraud-rule build around the behavioural scores flowing in from day one."
— **AR-08**

This compounds problem 3: not only is the underlying approval weak, the commitment has also vanished from the document that would actually bind Elva.

**8. Sanctions screening volume silently cut from 60,000/day to 30,000/day**
> "Name and sanctions screening is sized at up to sixty thousand checks a day, comfortably above your forecast peak."
— **AR-04**

versus

> "3.1 Elva will screen customer and beneficiary names against sanctions lists at volumes of up to 30,000 screenings per day."
— **AR-06**

No document explains or flags this reduction to the customer. It matters because the customer's own current forecast has since moved up, not down:
> "Peak-day modelling now puts us at around 45,000 name screenings, so the sizing in the proposal matters to us."
— **AR-08**
